sources.text: U.S. Department of Agriculture, FoodData Central — "Bananas, raw" (nutrient values per 100 g).

Phillips KM, McGinty RC, Couture G, Pehrsson PR, McKillop K, Fukagawa NK, "Dietary fiber, starch, and sugars in bananas at different stages of ripeness in the retail market," PLOS ONE 16(7): e0253366 (2021). Fiber measured by the method that captures resistant starch was ~18 g/100 g in unripe fruit, 4-5 g/100 g when ripe and ~2 g/100 g when overripe.
"In vitro examination of starch digestibility of Saba banana: impact of maturity and physical properties of digesta," Scientific Reports (Nature, 2020).
"Analysis of resistant starch degradation in postharvest ripening of two banana cultivars: focus on starch structure and amylases," Postharvest Biology and Technology (2016).
Hermansen K. et al., "Influence of ripeness of banana on the blood glucose and insulin response in type 2 diabetic subjects," Diabetic Medicine (1992), PubMed PMID 1395467.
"Bananas: Nutrition and possible health benefits" (medically reviewed), Healthline.
National Headache Foundation, "Low-Tyramine Diet for Individuals with Headache or Migraine."
U.S. Food and Drug Administration, "Mycotoxins" (patulin and other mould toxins in fruit).
USDA mould guidance, summarized by Tufts Health & Nutrition Letter, "Cutting away mold on fruit: is it safe?" (soft, high-moisture produce should be discarded entirely if mouldy).
"Acute consumption of resistant starch reduces food intake" and related work on native (unripe) banana starch lowering glycemic and insulin responses, PMC (NIH).
National Kidney Foundation, "Potassium in your CKD diet" and "Nutrition and kidney disease" (bananas are a high-potassium food to limit if advised).
Monash University FODMAP, "Bananas re-tested" (firm/unripe bananas are low-FODMAP; ripe and overripe bananas are higher in fructans and tolerated only in small servings).
Allergy & Asthma Network, "Latex allergy and foods" (latex-fruit syndrome; banana is a high cross-reactivity food to avoid for those affected).

Gibson GR, Hutkins R, Sanders ME, et al., "Expert consensus document: The International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) consensus statement on the definition and scope of prebiotics," Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology 14(8):491-502 (2017). Defines a prebiotic as "a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit."

"Short Chain Fatty Acids in the Colon and Peripheral Tissues: A Focus on Butyrate, Colon Cancer, Obesity and Insulin Resistance," PMC (NIH). Fermentation of resistant starch and other fibre in the colon produces short-chain fatty acids; butyrate is the main fuel of the cells lining the colon.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration, "Daily Value on the Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels" (Daily Value for dietary fibre: 28 g).
